description: Plain text with no markup counts identically to a Unicode-code-point-aware strlen.
Two paragraphs with no whitespace between them in the source concatenate directly, matching a browser's textContent (not html_to_text's inserted blank-line separator).
List items with no whitespace between them in the source concatenate directly, matching textContent (not html_to_text's bullet markers).
A real editor's serialised inter-element newline is a genuine DOM text node and counts, matching a browser's textContent exactly.
Three inter-element newlines in a real editor's serialised list markup are each a genuine text node and count.
contributes no character of its own, matching a browser's textContent.
Fully empty input is zero.
An empty rich-text editor shell serialises to markup, not an empty string, but still counts as zero.
The other common empty-editor shell shape also counts as zero.
Counted in Unicode code points, not bytes: multibyte accented characters and a 4-byte emoji outside the BMP each count as one character.
NBSP between two words is visible content and counts as one character - only a response that is ENTIRELY invisible characters is treated as empty.
Unwrapped bold/emphasis markup already agreed with html_to_text before this change; confirms no regression.
A named HTML entity decodes to its single character in the DOM text node.
Named entities for angle brackets decode to literal '<' and '>' characters, not markup.
A numeric character reference decodes to its single Unicode character.
An unclosed tag is auto-closed by the lenient HTML parser; the visible text is unaffected.
Mismatched closing tag order is repaired by the lenient HTML parser; only the visible text counts.
A '<' not followed by a valid tag name is literal text, not a tag start.
A bare '&' not matching a known entity/character-reference pattern is literal text.
ASCII whitespace-only input is visually empty.
A lone NBSP renders as an invisible gap; per the new emptiness rule it does not satisfy minchars/completion on its own (regression fixture for R4-01 - this was 1, not 0, before this change).
Multiple NBSP characters with nothing else are still visually empty.
Zero-width space/joiners, the word joiner, and a stray BOM never render anything and count as visually empty.
A mix of ASCII whitespace, NBSP, and a zero-width character with no visible character anywhere is still visually empty.

One visible character surrounded by ordinary spaces is not visually empty, so the raw count (including the surrounding spaces) is returned unchanged - only the fully-empty boundary is new, not interior counting.
A visible character between NBSP and a zero-width character is not visually empty either; the raw count includes all three characters.
A lone ideographic space (U+3000, common in CJK-input paste) is a Unicode Space_Separator stripped by JS's native String.trim(), so PHP's regex must include it too or the two sides disagree.
An em space (U+2003, from the U+2000-U+200A Unicode space block, realistic from a Word paste) is likewise stripped by native trim() and must be covered on the PHP side.
The Unicode line separator (U+2028) is an ECMAScript LineTerminator, also stripped by native trim(), and must be covered on the PHP side.
